inline_comments.comment: RST section-hierarchy bug: 'Selecting a part of a trajectory' uses `.` (dots) as its underline character, but every other section at the same logical level — 'Basic controls' (line 59), 'Plotting data from the command line' (line 95), 'Configuring the GUI' (line 111), and 'Polling the GUI' (line 179) — uses `-` (dashes). In reStructuredText the hierarchy is determined by the first occurrence of each underline character in the document. Because `...` appears before `-`, Sphinx will treat `...` as the higher sub-level and `-` as a deeper sub-level, which means 'Basic controls', 'Plotting data', 'Configuring the GUI', and 'Polling the GUI' will all be rendered as children of 'Selecting a part of a trajectory' rather than as siblings. Change the underline on line 36 from `................................` to `--------------------------------` (dashes) to match the other sections.

Lines 24–26 are RST comments (`.. or` and `.. >>> view(atoms, repeat=(3, 3, 2))`), so the `repeat` usage example is silently omitted from the rendered documentation. The `view(atoms, repeat=(3, 3, 2))` call is a frequently-used feature. If the example is still valid, remove the `.. ` prefixes to expose it; if it was deliberately suppressed, delete these lines entirely to avoid confusing future editors.

The 'four atoms' row in the selection table no longer mentions that the atoms must be selected sequentially for the dihedral angle to be well-defined. The previous version explicitly said 'four atoms, selected sequentially' and 'the angle between bonds 12 and 34', making it clear that atom order matters. Without this qualifier a user could select four atoms in any order and be confused by the result. Consider adding a note such as 'four atoms (selected in order)' to restore that guidance.

The blank line after `.. attention::` (line 6) contains four trailing spaces. Trailing whitespace on otherwise-blank lines is a common source of linting warnings and can cause subtle reStructuredText parsing issues. It should be an empty line with no spaces.

'Delete selected atoms' (lines 75–77) has only the keyboard shortcut with no prose description, unlike every other entry in the file. Even a single-sentence description such as 'Permanently removes all currently selected atoms from the image.' keeps the section consistent and useful to users who read the docs rather than the tooltip.
Trailing whitespace at the end of line 15: `...can be used to create the ` has a trailing space before the newline. This should be trimmed.
Grammar error: 'These constraints will be then be saved to a file' (line 69) has a double 'be'. Should read: 'These constraints will then be saved to a file'.

Lines 119–121 are commented-out RST (`.. ::` / `..   $ ase gui --interpolate 3 ...`), leaving dead content in the source. If the `--interpolate` command is still a valid and useful way to set up a NEB path it should be uncommented; if it is outdated or moved elsewhere it should be deleted. Leaving it as a silent comment is the worst of both options — it is invisible to readers but a maintenance burden for future editors.

The label option listed as 'Chemical symbol' (line 55) does not match the menu string in `gui.py`, which reads `_('_Element symbol')`. Users who look for 'Chemical symbol' in the GUI menu will not find an exact match. Similarly, 'Magnetic moment' (singular, line 54) differs from `_('_Magnetic moments')` (plural) in the code. Aligning the documentation labels with the exact menu strings would reduce confusion.
Typo: 'Depending on you operating system' should be 'Depending on your operating system'.

general_comments.comment: The 'Writing files' section that existed in the old `basics.rst` — which showed `ase gui -n -1 a*.traj -o new.traj` and listed the supported output formats (`traj`, `xyz`, `cube`, `pdb`, `eps`, `png`, `pov`) — was removed and does not appear to have been moved anywhere else in the GUI documentation. Users who want to know how to export files from the CLI will now need to fall back on `ase gui -h` or the `ase.io` module docs. If this is intentional, a brief cross-reference from the GUI docs to the relevant section of the CLI or IO documentation would help readers who expect to find this information here.

The capitalization fixes in `ase/gui/gui.py` (e.g. 'Show _Labels' → 'Show _labels', 'Quick Info …' → 'Quick info …') are sensible and internally consistent. It is worth noting that these changes affect the human-visible menu strings inside the `_(...)` gettext calls, which means any existing translation catalogues (`.po`/`.mo` files) that have entries for the old capitalised strings will no longer match and those menu items will fall back to the English source string until the catalogues are updated. If the project ships translations, the translation template (`.pot` file) should be regenerated as part of this change.
